DESCRIPTION: Card and loan payments have three write paths (the payment form, the account page and recurring generation) and only some of them keep `credit_card_payments` and the statement in step. The LED-146, LED-145 and LED-114 retros listed the gaps. Phases and the decision register are in epics-15-19-build-order.md.

SUMMARY: Recurring transfers to a card run the statement steps
USER_STORY: As a user with a recurring card payment, I want the statement to update when it posts, so the balance and the statement agree.
DESCRIPTION: `generateDueRecurring` (src/hooks/useTransactions.ts:324, called from src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:203). Found by LED-146 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-146-one-card-payment-path.md). Observed: A recurring transfer whose destination is a card is generated as a plain transfer; the statement steps `useCardPayment` runs (`credit_card_payments`, src/hooks/useCardPayment.ts:51) are skipped. Suggested fix: When a generated row is a transfer to a card, run the same path, or explain why it is not needed (a card payment is a transfer, `rules/card-payment-is-a-transfer.md`). Keep the queue and the "one row per due date" behaviour.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A due recurring transfer to a card creates the same records a manual payment does; (b) generating twice creates them once; (c) balances agree with the statement; (d) offline behaviour is unchanged; (e) a test on the decision of which rows take the card path.

SUMMARY: Editing or deleting a card payment keeps the statement in step
USER_STORY: As a user, I want to correct a card payment without leaving a stale statement behind, so the card page stays true.
DESCRIPTION: Edit and delete of a card-payment transaction (src/pages/AccountTransactionsPage.tsx writes `credit_card_payments` at line 315; the edit and delete paths do not). Found by LED-146 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-146-one-card-payment-path.md) and the phase 10 retro (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-epics-8-13-phase-10-design-parity.md); "as before". Observed: Changing the amount or deleting the transfer leaves the `credit_card_payments` row and the statement as they were. Suggested fix: One invoker function (`knowledge/patterns/atomic-write-as-an-invoker-function.md`) that updates or removes both records in one transaction; confirm on a local database that the account-balance triggers net correctly.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Editing the amount updates the statement row; (b) deleting removes it and the balances net to zero; (c) a failed write leaves both records unchanged (`partial-failure-with-fix.md`); (d) a migration (if any) applies to an empty database and passes the CI `db` job; (e) tests; (f) checked live on a card with two payments.

SUMMARY: Payment history refreshes after a payment from the global modal
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a payment I just made to show on the card page, so I do not reload to see it.
DESCRIPTION: src/pages/AccountTransactionsPage.tsx (payment history). Found by LED-146 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-146-one-card-payment-path.md). Observed: The history refreshes only when the payment is made on that page; one made from the global modal shows after a reload. Suggested fix: Refetch on the same signal the transaction list uses (`knowledge/patterns/hook-instances-do-not-share-state.md`), not a second listener.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Pay from the global modal while the card page is open: the row appears; (b) no extra request when nothing changed; (c) no flash of the empty state (`resolveLoadState`).

SUMMARY: Fixing a queued card payment does not need a connection
USER_STORY: As an offline user, I want to fix a queued card payment, so a typo does not block the queue.
DESCRIPTION: The Fix action on a failed queue item (`src/lib/queueState.ts` and the queue review sheet). Found by LED-146 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-146-one-card-payment-path.md). Observed: Fix on a queued payment reruns the statement steps, which need a connection. Suggested fix: Edit the queued payload only; run the statement steps when it drains (`knowledge/patterns/offline-queue-conflict-handling.md`).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Offline, Fix on a queued card payment opens and saves; (b) the statement steps run once on drain; (c) a test in `queueState` for the edited payload; (d) checked with the network blocked.

SUMMARY: Card dialog subtitle and category counts for card payments
USER_STORY: As a user, I want the card dialog to describe what it does, so the copy matches LED-146.
DESCRIPTION: `src/lib/kindMenu.ts:111` reads "Posts as an expense against the card · type locked". A card payment has been a transfer since LED-146 (`rules/card-payment-is-a-transfer.md`). Found by LED-114 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-114-card-payments-not-spending.md) and the phase 13 retro (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-epics-8-13-phase-13-decision-gated.md). Also: category filter counts and the Categories page usage were not re-read for card payments (they use the same expense filter). Suggested fix: Reword the line and its test; re-read the two counts with a card payment present.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The subtitle says the payment is a transfer; (b) the kind menu test is updated; (c) with one card payment, Categories counts and the category filter counts do not include it; (d) checked at 1280 and 390.

SUMMARY: Pay now for a past loan bill defaults to today
USER_STORY: As a user paying a late loan bill, I want the payment dated when I make it, so the split matches what is owed today.
DESCRIPTION: Home Upcoming Bills, Pay now (src/components/dashboard/DashboardUpcomingBillsCard.tsx:89; prefill in src/hooks/useDashboardData.ts:71). Found by LED-145 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-145-home-pay-now.md). Observed: Pay now for a loan bill in the past dates the payment on the old due date. `rules/loan-payment-date-decides-its-split.md`: the date decides the split, so the old date allocates as if the payment had been on time. Recommendation: prefill today for a past bill, keep the due date for a future one, and let the user change it. Decision inside the ticket, not blocking. Fallback: as is.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A past-due Pay now opens on today's date; (b) a future bill keeps its due date; (c) the allocation preview (LED-107) uses the date shown; (d) a unit test on the prefill; (e) LED-173 (overdue rows) still holds.
